primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 3 deficiency due to HSD17B3 loss of function
mechanism: HSD17B3 is expressed predominantly in the testes and catalyzes the NADPH-dependent conversion of androstenedione to testosterone. Loss of enzyme activity reduces testicular testosterone production and causes undervirilization in 46,XY individuals.
vignette: A 15-year-old adolescent raised as female is evaluated for absent menses. Examination shows scant pubic hair, no uterus on pelvic ultrasound, and bilateral inguinal testes. Karyotype is 46,XY. Laboratory studies after hCG stimulation show a markedly elevated androstenedione concentration with relatively low testosterone. Genetic testing identifies biallelic HSD17B3 variants.
lead: Which of the following steroid conversions is directly impaired in this patient?
distractor_notes: Testosterone-to-DHT conversion is catalyzed by 5-alpha-reductase, not HSD17B3.
The first mitochondrial steroidogenic step from cholesterol to pregnenolone is catalyzed by CYP11A1 after StAR-mediated cholesterol delivery.
DHEA to androstenedione is catalyzed primarily by 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, not HSD17B3.
key_expl: 17β-HSD3, encoded by HSD17B3, is a testis-predominant enzyme that reduces androstenedione to testosterone using NADPH. Deficiency therefore produces a low testosterone-to-androstenedione ratio and 46,XY undervirilization.
objective: Identify androstenedione-to-testosterone conversion as the reaction catalyzed by testicular 17β-HSD3.
